description.narrative: In the long-term, the action will strengthen the contribution of culture to sustainable development, notably through heritage-based tourism development, diversifying tourism products and delivering high-quality visitor experiences along the Silk Roads heritage corridors in the participating countries. The adaptation of the Training Handbook for Silk Road Heritage Guides to include information about ICH in CA was completed. The adapted Handbook was printed hard copies were distributed among tourism guides tourism associations and other key stakeholders of CA countries. The ecopy of the Handbook is available for public at httpsunesdoc.unesco.orgark48223pf0000374500The Core Module of the training manual Cultural Heritage Specialist Guide Training and Certification Programme for UNESCO World Heritage Sites was translated from English into Farsi. The Site Module for 8 identified Iranian World Heritage Sites related to the training manual of Cultural Heritage Specialist Guide Training and Certification Programme for UNESCO World Heritage Sites is developed by Iranian Ministry of Cultural Heritage Tourism and Handicrafts and is under assessment by associated organizations to attain required national approvals for publication based on newly established national protocols by the Government.

Overall 303 trainees participated in the capacitybuilding activities for ICH heritage bearers from Afghanistan Tajikistan Uzbekistan.The participants received an opportunity to enhance their craftsmanship skills and develop entrepreneurial skills.In UzbekistanThe theoretical and practical trainings on traditional craftsmanship ethnodesign and entrepreneurship were conducted from 12 to 22 October 2021 in Margilan to developstrengthen the traditional skills and knowledge in the field of embroidery carpetweaving ethnodesign natural dyeing blockprinting and craft entrepreneurship for 63 participants including women and youth from all the regions of Uzbekistan. Overall 193 craftspeople 92.7 women 73 men were introduced to the background role and importance of traditional forms of craftsmanship and given practical trainings on carpet weaving embroidery ceramics and ethnodesign out of 193 63 craftspeople were trained during the reporting period Year 4.The ICH bearers were trained on entrepreneurship including marketing legal aspects social media communication photo skills etc. in the field of craftsmanship thus developing their skills in promoting their crafts products in local and world markets.In Tajikistan The practical training on product development and Social Media Marketing was organized for 20 artisan women in Khujand city Tajikistan in the period from 11 to 16 July 2022 followed by a mentorship programme launched in August 2022. The participants have improved their skills on producing traditional products and developed their entrepreneurial skills.

The outcomes of the report recommendations and action plan were presented to key stakeholders from Tajikistan and ICH experts from CA 38 participants overall. Then the proofreading and development of the design will be launched.

comment.narrative: 8 component sites of TianShan corridor in Kazakhstan the Management Plans for the component sites are outdated. TianShan corridor is not included as WH property in the State Programme of Tourism Development for 20192025 out of 11 component only 1 site Akyrtas is included in the State Programme.3 component sites of TianShan corridor in Kyrgyzstan Management Plans for the cultural sites are outdated. TianShan corridor is not included as WH property in the Programme of Tourism Development for 20192023 although need for development of cultural tourism is noted. Out of 3 component sites of the TianShan corridor only Burana is mentioned in the Programme.Tajik National Park Tajikistan included in the recently developed Tourism Development Strategy of Tajikistan while the Management Plan for the Tajik National Park is outdated.Bogbonli mosque Itchan kala Khiva Uzbekistan In 20152016 the draft Management Plan of Itchan kala was developed and in 2017 was officially presented to the local government and Ministry of Culture.
